reactions: S2(wet, trapped) + S15(unworked pocket) under X3 -> S6(phase to gas), Load fail -> E1: pot cracks from steam pressure

missing.why: Throwing a pot on a wheel is plastic forming of one mass, not motion, force-damage, or joining two things; X5's 'build' is the closest fit and is a stretch.

S8's contents/pressure is defined for hollow things, and Load's pressure sources are contents, P22 and S9-gas; a moisture pocket trapped inside solid clay has to stretch one of these beyond what is stated.

lost: The steam-pressure mechanism that cracks the pot is only reachable by stretching S8 (hollow-thing contents and pressure) onto a solid material's internal defect, and the throwing step has no clean process id.

missing.why: S4 integrity only runs whole, cracked, broken, in pieces; there is no state for plastic deformation like warping, which the quenched blade and its straightening both need.

Reforging by heating near melting and hammering two pieces into one isn't clearly one of X5's stated strength sources (stickiness, friction, flexibility, fit, care); 'graft' is the nearest verb and is a stretch from its biological sense.

Warping from quenching too fast and at an angle needs uneven cooling across one instance; section 8 says detail inside one instance isn't tracked (coverage is one number), and this scenario's outcome turns on exactly that.

lost: There is no state for 'bent but not broken,' so the warp from an angled quench and the cold-straightening that follows can only be gestured at with S4's whole/cracked/broken levels, not actually expressed.

missing.why: M4 states S9's effects as noxiousness-when-eaten, scent, and (sealed, sugary) potency and gas. It says nothing about S9 weakening a joined bond, so hair-slip has to stretch R4 (whose stated drift causes are use, drying and wet) beyond what is given.

lost: Hair-slip is only expressed by stretching R4's joined-to strength to also respond to contamination, which M4 never grants.

missing.why: X7 lists 'ferment' and 'rot' as separate verbs, but the only rot/growth-tracking state is S9, and M4 says contamination uniformly adds noxiousness. There is no way to race a wanted ferment against a spoiling contamination on the same wort without S9 also making the good outcome noxious.

lost: The balance the whole scenario turns on, the same warmth helping the wanted process and the unwanted one, cannot be expressed because only one contamination scalar exists and its one stated effect is uniformly bad.

missing.why: Volume increase from yeast gas has no clean home: P22 swell is anchored to freezing and soaking only, and S9/M4's contamination effects are food-safety framed (noxiousness, scent), not gas-driven volume growth.

lost: Dough's rise is only reachable by stretching P22 (freeze/soak swell) to also cover fermentation gas, which it is not defined for.

missing.why: The lintel sagging under its own weight needs an intermediate deformed-but-whole state; S4 integrity only runs whole, cracked, broken, in pieces, with nothing between whole and cracked for a slow bend.

lost: The joints loosening (R4 drifting with drying, explicitly granted) is well covered, but the lintel's resulting sag has no state to land in.

missing.why: M4's stated contamination effects are noxiousness-when-eaten, scent, and (sealed, sugary) potency and gas. Nothing states S9 reducing a material's structural strength, which the rotten rafter's collapse needs.

lost: The rafter losing load-bearing strength from rot has to assume an effect that S9's one modifier rule never grants.

missing.why: Same gap as the rafter: M4 gives S9 no stated effect on hardness, toughness or mass, so a rotten fence rail failing under a goat's weight has to assume an unstated strength loss.

lost: The rail's rot-driven weakness, hidden under whitewash and found only when it gives way, fits S7/S15/Load's design well; the rot-to-weaker-wood link itself is unstated.

missing.why: Self-heating of damp, packed grain needs S9's growth to raise S1 temperature; M4 only grants noxiousness, scent, and (sealed, sugary) potency and gas, not a temperature effect.

lost: The grain heating itself from its own dampness, the scenario's whole point, has no modifier rule connecting S9 to S1.

effects: E5:bucket to bottom (X1 on what it held)

missing.why: B1's need list (hunger, thirst, air, rest, warmth, money, safety, company) has no entry for a producing animal's milk buildup, so the goat's discomfort from missed milking, and its relief, have no body condition to shift.

lost: The goat's suffering and relief, the thing the scenario's cost is actually measured in, has no B1 need or body condition to attach to.
